paragraphs: In Shabbat 23a he disagrees with Rav Avya; Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.
In Yevamot 102a, Rav Nechemyah asks Rabbah a question. Tosafot there cites an early authority who says the name should read Nechemyah bar Baruch.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The two proposed alternatives concern separate passages: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak in Shabbat 23a, attributed by Hyman to דק״ס (conventionally Dikdukei Soferim), and Nechemyah bar Baruch in Yevamot 102a, attributed to an unnamed early authority cited in Tosafot. They are not combined into a single identity.
חד מקמאי means “an early authority”; no particular author is named. Hyman’s alternative Nechemyah bar Baruch has no Rav title, so none is added. The locators retain the printed folio sides.
